requirements.requirement: The shared identity dataops exists on both nodes with UID and GID 4500.
requirements.summary: Both nodes directly report dataops:x:4500:4500 and group dataops with GID 4500; node2 reconfirms the identity after restart.

requirements.requirement: node1 exports /srv/nfs/shared as a writable NFS share, owned by dataops:dataops with mode 2770.
requirements.summary: The directory has numeric ownership 4500:4500 and mode 2770. The NFS service is active, the export is writable and restricted to node2, and the same state is directly observed after node1 restarts.

requirements.requirement: node2 mounts node1's exported directory at /mnt/shared.
requirements.summary: findmnt directly shows /mnt/shared mounted read-write from node1 using NFSv4.2. The fstab entry is present, and the mount is recovered after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Files created from either node retain consistent dataops ownership and permissions and are accessible through the share.
requirements.summary: Files created independently on node1 and node2 are read from the opposite node and report dataops:dataops, UID/GID 4500, and mode 660. A new file created after both restarts is also observed on node1 with the same ownership and mode.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The NFS share is active and writable, node2 has the correct live mount, both systems use dataops UID/GID 4500, and cross-node file tests demonstrate consistent ownership and permissions. Persistence and recovery were additionally demonstrated through complete, independently corroborated restarts of both nodes.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, identity and directory creation, SELinux/export/firewall configuration, persistent mounting, bounded test-file creation, and restarts all had clear roles in implementing or verifying the requested share. The test files remained as bounded functional evidence. Final snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, and only task-related NFS/RPC listeners. Both required restart protocols are complete: each node has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state; the fixed lifecycle boot observations independently agree.
